audit.comparability: non-comparable baseline target/method schema; clean current run establishes the WASM-3.0 eight-actor baseline

findings.title: Startup and schema application dominate the shared runtime floor
findings.evidence: The final empty actor is 1,946,039 bytes. Named attribution retains 1,066,322 bytes from startup_driver_attempt in the typed actor and 1,009,362 bytes in the SQL actor; lower_application_candidates retains 271,360 and 247,799 bytes respectively.
findings.impact: A broad cleanup here could reduce every generated canister, while a mistaken split or duplicated helper could grow every canister and weaken startup correctness.
findings.disposition: OWNER AUDIT COMPLETE; BOUNDED EXPERIMENT ONLY
findings.audit_result: Generated proposals always carry an empty removal set, but initial and existing-head lowering, canonical proposal composition and the singular core admission/publication authority are all lifecycle-required.
findings.recommended_experiment: Measure one private generated no-removal lowering contract beneath the existing core authority; reject it if any minimum actor saves less than 32 KiB final raw Wasm or startup instructions regress.
rejected_alternatives: bypass generated fragment decoding or canonical proposal composition
split initial installation from existing-head reconciliation
merge removal representations only to share sort monomorphs
treat facade source duplication as measured Wasm duplication
findings.trigger: Only after a new footprint minor is explicitly authorized; the SQL-ingress owner audit is the next read-only closeout opportunity.

findings.title: The SQL ingress retains a 1.125 MB execution closure
findings.evidence: Final-artifact dominators attribute 1,125,250 bytes, 34.23% of one_entity_sql_query, to query_one_entity_sql. The SQL actor is 1,169,747 bytes larger than the typed actor, but that cross-actor subtraction remains directional by contract.
findings.impact: The largest SQL-only opportunity is flow-wide frontend/executor retention, not another narrow exact aggregate branch.
findings.trigger: Before the next SQL performance or Wasm optimization design selects a production owner.

findings.title: Sort monomorphization is the largest generic-bloat family
findings.evidence: Named Twiggy estimates 113,858 bytes across four sort families in the typed actor, 171,947 in SQL, and 148,653 in the ten-entity actor.
findings.impact: The signal is broad but not directly removable because the instances carry different types and ordering semantics; type erasure may exchange bytes for instructions and complexity.
findings.trigger: A concrete existing sort owner can be shared without allocation, indirect dispatch, semantic change or query regression.
